text:
mira: quick thought  we should make checkpoint emission adaptive to client backpressure and token-rate patterns, not strictly periodic. reduces unnecessary checkpoints for fast clients and gives slower clients more anchors.

sam: interesting. how would gateway/worker negotiate that?
mira: propose a light negotiation handshake at stream start: client sends preferred checkpoint hint (none|sparse|balanced|aggressive) and gateway exposes client-observed egress pacing. workers then emit frames aligned to the negotiated cadence.

raj: so negotiation flow looks like: client -> gateway: CheckpointHint, gateway attaches ObservedPacingHint to backend call, backend chooses emission strategy and includes emitted cadence in-progress frames?
mira: exactly. minimal wire sketch below.

```
// initial headers (at stream open)
X-Checkpoint-Hint: balanced   // client hint
X-GW-Pacing-Estimate: 120rps // gateway observed outgoing token rate (opt)

// in-stream progress frame (canonical)
CHK v1 { seq: u64, bytes: u64, tokens: u32, cadence: "sparse|balanced|aggressive", crc32: hex }
```

kevin: nice. cadence field helps gateway choose when to persist anchors and when to request resume. default fallback if absent: balanced.

lina: concerns: this adds policy surface. who owns cadence decisions? app teams might game it (e.g., aggressive to reduce duplicate work but cause more metadata churn).
mira: propose server-side enforcement: gateway can clamp requested cadence by route config or tenant tier. baseline: free-tier -> sparse, default -> balanced, enterprise -> configurable aggressive allowed.

julia: op safety: adaptive checkpoints mean variable storage churn. gateway should store only last checkpoint per stream, but cadence controls emit frequency; that's fine. also add a soft-rate limit on per-gateway checkpoint writes per-second to protect control plane.

sam: what about observability? we need metrics showing mismatches between client hint and actual emitted cadence so we can tune defaults.
mira: good call. metrics: checkpoint_hint_distribution, emitted_cadence_breakdown, resume_attempts_by_cadence, resume_success_by_cadence. plus a trace span when negotiation differs.

raj: failure modes: if gateway dies before checkpoint persisted, resume unavailable. TTL still applies. Also partial-frame delivery edge-case still stands. keep CRC requirement.

kevin: rollout plan: 1) add header parsing in gateway + store hint in routing metadata 2) backend: implement cadence-aware emitter, include cadence in frames 3) gateway: persist last-checkpoint + cadence + TTL, expose metrics 4) pilot with internal teams and an opt-in feature flag

lina: security question: are any of these fields sensitive? no. but we must ensure cadences don't leak tenant load patterns beyond normal telemetry. keep minimal.

mira: ops-bot posted RFC stub: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/adaptive-checkpointing (auto)
ops-bot: Mira posted: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/adaptive-checkpointing 

sam: +1 to prototype. can runtime and serving pair up for a short spike to measure memory and resume success differences across cadences?
mira: scheduling a 30min spike next week. default negotiation: if client omits hint, gateway sets balanced; route config can override. TTL: default 30s, configurable.

raj: +1. also add a debug-mode header to force exact cadence for testing: X-Debug-Force-Cadence. gated behind flags.

kevin: tagging @runtime @serving @product for awareness.

julia: one more: add a heuristics hook so backend can increase cadence near sentence boundaries even if sparse was chosen. better UX without global churn.
mira: great idea  will add to RFC checklist.
